BC contains everything in AP Calculus AB plus the additional topics below — advanced integration, logistic models and Euler's method, parametric, polar and vector functions, and the full theory of sequences and series. The six BC chapters, worked free-response questions, and a 50-question practice exam are all here.

The exam format matches AB (multiple choice 50%, free response 50%), and a BC result also reports an AB subscore.

label.en: ⏱️ AP Calculus BC Exam Breakdown & Timing Strategy

body.en:
• Section I: Multiple Choice (50% of score, 45 questions, 105 min):
    • Part A (60 min, 30 questions, NO calculator): ~27 AB questions + ~3 BC questions. Pacing: 2 min/question.
    • Part B (45 min, 15 questions, Graphing calculator required): ~9 AB questions + ~6 BC questions. Pacing: 3 min/question.
  • Section II: Free Response (50% of score, 6 questions, 90 min):
    • Part A (30 min, 2 questions, Graphing calculator required): Typically Question 1 (Rate in/out or area/volume) and Question 2 (Parametric/vector motion).
    • Part B (60 min, 4 questions, NO calculator): Questions 3–5 cover differential equations/Euler, FTC graph analysis, and polar area; Question 6 is always Taylor Series & Error Bounds.
  • BC Scoring Thresholds: A composite score of roughly 62–66% earns a 5 on AP Calculus BC, and ~50–55% earns a 4. High performance on core AB topics combined with harvesting method points on Taylor series guarantees top scores.

label.en: 💡 The Two Giant BC-Exclusive Capstone Pillars

body.en:
• Unit 9: Parametric, Polar & Vector Calculus (11–12% of exam):
    Extends single-variable calculus to curves in the plane: parametric slope \( \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} \), second derivative \( \frac{(dy/dx)'}{dx/dt} \), vector velocity \( \vec{v}(t) = \langle x', y' \rangle \), scalar speed \( \|\vec{v}\| = \sqrt{(x')^2+(y')^2} \), arc length, and polar area \( \frac{1}{2}\int r^2\,d\theta \).
  • Unit 10: Infinite Sequences & Series (17–18% of exam):
    The most challenging unit on the exam: convergence tests (Geometric, p-Series, Ratio, Limit Comparison, Alternating Series), absolute vs. conditional convergence, power series intervals of convergence, Taylor and Maclaurin polynomial constructions, and error bounding (Alternating Series Error vs. Lagrange Error Bound).

caption.en: AP Calculus BC exam topic distribution across primary units and AB/BC split. Core AB topics account for ~60% of the composite score (and the AB Subscore), while BC-exclusive topics (Integration techniques, Euler/Logistic, Parametric/Polar/Vector, and Infinite Series) comprise the remaining ~40%.

question.en: Section I of AP Calculus BC consists of 45 Multiple Choice questions (Part A: 30 non-calculator questions in 60 minutes; Part B: 15 calculator-active questions in 45 minutes). Calculate the average time allocated per question for Part A versus Part B in minutes.

solution.en: For Part A: \(\frac{60\text{ minutes}}{30\text{ questions}} = 2.0\text{ minutes per question}\). For Part B: \(\frac{45\text{ minutes}}{15\text{ questions}} = 3.0\text{ minutes per question}\). Part B grants 50% more time per question because graphing calculator input and multi-step interpretation are required.
